A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SePO research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and v2 Appendices A–J support comparison, including matching material relocated from v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, token-selection and data-scale experiments, and weak-to-strong evaluations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model comparisons, larger-oracle experiments, computational measurements, hyperparameter experiments, and token-selection case studies.

M1.justification: v2 adds a contrastive margin λ to the SePO objective, absent from v1 Equation 26. Appendix B and Algorithm 1 introduce character-based transfer of selected tokens across vocabularies, extending the procedure beyond v1's explicitly shared-tokenizer setting.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraChat-200K, UltraFeedback, HH-RLHF, and QA-Feedback, with Arena-Hard, AlpacaEval 2.0, and MT-Bench evaluations. The QA reward analysis moves to v2 Appendix D/Figure 6. Added model configurations do not introduce different datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds TDPO, SparsePO, and the random-token control SePO-rand to the retained DPO, IPO, RRHF, and SimPO comparisons. Appendix Table 7 also adds TDPO and SePO-rand to the earlier MT-Bench comparison. The HH-RLHF comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA3-Base-8B and LLaMA3-Instruct-8B evaluations, cross-tokenizer supervision, and oracle configurations up to 12B rather than v1's 1.4B maximum. It introduces GPU-hour measurements and γ/λ sweep protocols. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a random-selection control testing the value of oracle selection, larger-oracle scaling analysis, γ/λ sensitivity experiments, computational-overhead analysis, and two token-selection case studies. Most original analyses remain, although the TinyLLaMA panel of the token-selection-ratio experiment is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 8 adds error bars and explicitly reports three runs per hyperparameter setting. The earlier three-sampling averages for the data-scale experiment are retained in Figure 4. The new error bars' statistical meaning is unspecified, and no seed values or formal significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial model, comparator, timing, scaling, and sensitivity results. Existing MT-Bench values also change, including LLaMA2-Chat-13B SePO from 6.36 to 6.86; these are revised results rather than established same-procedure gains because the objective changes. TinyLLaMA's comprehensive Arena-Hard/AlpacaEval table entries disappear, while its MT-Bench results remain.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds a token-level gradient derivation and the sample-weighting expression in Equations 31–32. The original assumption, two theorems, and their substantive proofs are retained; moving proofs to Appendix C and adding main-text proof sketches do not themselves constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explicit claim of up to 60% lower GPU training time and extend the main performance claim to six policy models. The central DPO-based selective-alignment contribution, 30% token claim, and 16.8× weak-to-strong claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning suffix truncation and amortized oracle costs, diminishing returns from larger oracles, margin sensitivity, and token-selection mechanisms. The shared-vocabulary limitation is replaced by cross-vocabulary support, while manually determined token-selection ratios become an explicit limitation. The earlier math/coding qualification remains in Appendix H.

D1.justification: v2 adds hardware/software, optimizer, epochs, batch sizes, learning rates, and dataset splits in Table 8; baseline hyperparameter ranges in Table 6; the reward-annotation prompt; and truncation details. It also adds a project/code hyperlink. These substantially expand documentation beyond v1 without proving changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds focused discussion of SparsePO, Inverse-Q*, and T-reg, with explicit comparisons concerning optimization, oracle reuse, and weak-to-strong supervision. LLaMA3 and FlashAttention-2 references are also added. The original three-part research framing and central novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: Detailed proofs, related work, and weak-to-strong background move into appendices, accompanied by rewritten main-text summaries and proof sketches. The former Discussion becomes separate Conclusion and Limitations sections. Related-work rewriting and the extensive main-text/appendix reorganization substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned into side-by-side model blocks with GPU-hour columns, while expanded MT-Bench category results appear separately in Table 7. The pipeline diagram is redrawn, existing figures are split or relocated, and new scaling/cost tables, hyperparameter plots, an algorithm display, and colored case-study figures are added.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses substantial gaps in v1 through directly relevant token-level baselines, a random-selection control, cross-vocabulary support, and detailed training and computational-cost documentation. These strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The gains outweigh reporting problems, including conflicting Pythia-2.8B SePO MT-Bench scores in Tables 1 and 7 (3.45 versus 3.65) and a scaling limitation inconsistent with the newly evaluated stronger oracles.
